facts.fact: Oracle News Daily reports Abdullah Kamara's memorandum saying Liberia currently lacks clear guardrails for how AI should be used or governed, and that the Ministry of Post & Telecommunications, the Liberia Telecommunications Authority and the National Security Agency have yet to establish AI-specific frameworks.

LBR.note: Only a recommendation for interim guidelines on public sector AI use; no government use is stated.

facts.fact: Oracle News Daily reports Abdullah Kamara's memorandum saying Liberia lacks clear guardrails on AI and recommending legislation to regulate high-risk AI applications.

LBR.note: No AI tool in a public sector system is stated.
The memorandum recommends a national AI policy and taskforce; it does not state that none exists or is being written.
No AI built or hosted in Liberia is stated; AI tools in use are said to be hosted abroad.
No training for civil servants is stated.
No data centre in Liberia is stated.
Data protection is raised as a risk; no law or bill is named.

facts.fact: Oracle News Daily says the Liberia Digital Transformation Project, chaired by Abdullah Kamara, trained 10,000 young Liberians in digital skills as promised by President Joseph Boakai.

LBR.note: No national ID system is described.
No data centre in Liberia is stated.
No school internet figure or curriculum rule is stated.
